title: Internal energy and energy transfers; Particle model and pressure

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Kinetic energy of particles
items.clue: The energy the particles have because they are moving, vibrating or rotating.

items.label: Heating
items.clue: An energy transfer that increases the energy of the particles that make up a system.

items.label: Internal energy
items.clue: The energy stored inside a system by the particles (atoms and molecules) that make up that system.

items.label: Potential energy of particles
items.clue: The energy stored because of the positions of the particles relative to one another and the forces between them.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the internal energy of a system?

options.text: The energy stored inside the system by its own particles
The temperature the system reaches when it is heated
The heat that flowed in and is now held inside
The energy the system gives out to its surroundings

questions.explanation: Energy is stored inside a system by the particles (atoms and molecules) that make up the system, and that store is called internal energy.

questions.stem: When a substance is heated and its temperature increases, the size of that increase depends on which three things?

options.text: The volume, the type of material and the total time of heating
The mass, the final temperature and the energy supplied
The mass, the type of material and the energy input to it
The mass, the energy input and the type of container

questions.explanation: These are the three factors the specification lists for the increase in temperature.

questions.stem: What is meant by the latent heat of a substance?

options.text: The energy stored by a substance once it has melted
The energy that is needed for a substance to change state
The energy needed to raise a substance by one degree
The energy lost by a substance while its temperature is constant

questions.explanation: The specification calls the energy needed for a substance to change state its latent heat.

questions.stem: Which statement about the molecules of a gas is correct?

options.text: They are in constant random motion, and the temperature of the gas is related to their average kinetic energy.
They are in constant random motion, and the temperature of the gas is set by their total kinetic energy.
They all move at one single fixed speed, and the temperature of the gas is set by that shared speed.
They move along fixed repeating paths, and the temperature of the gas is set by their spacing.

questions.stem: The pressure of a gas produces a net force on the wall of its container. In which direction does that net force act?

options.text: At an angle that depends on the shape of the container.
Along the surface of the wall, in the direction of flow.
Straight down, because of the weight of the gas.
At right angles to the surface of the container wall.

questions.explanation: The specification states that the pressure produces a net force at right angles to the wall of the gas container, or any surface, because the sideways parts of the impacts cancel.

questions.stem: Internal energy is the total of which two energy stores of the particles in a system?

options.text: The chemical energy and the thermal energy of all the particles
The kinetic energy and the potential energy of the particles
The kinetic energy of every one of the particles, only
The kinetic energy stored as the particles move about

questions.explanation: Internal energy is the total kinetic energy and potential energy of all the particles that make up a system.

questions.stem: 1 kg of water and 1 kg of cooking oil are each supplied with 20 000 J. The oil ends up much hotter than the water. Why?

options.text: Equal masses given equal energy must reach equal temperatures
The oil has a much higher specific heat capacity than water
The oil is thicker, so the heater warms it up quickly
Oil has a lower specific heat capacity than the water does

questions.explanation: The increase in temperature depends on the type of material; oil needs less energy per kilogram per degree Celsius.

questions.stem: Steam is produced steadily from boiling water at 100 °C. What happens to the energy that is supplied?

options.text: It raises the temperature of the water past 100 °C
It is stored in the heater until the boiling has finished
It changes the energy stored but not the temperature
It leaves the water's own internal energy unchanged

questions.explanation: During a change of state the energy supplied changes the internal energy of the substance, not its temperature.

questions.stem: A sealed container of gas is heated and the temperature of the gas rises. What happens to the molecules of the gas?

options.text: They all speed up by exactly the same amount and keep sharing one common speed.
Their average kinetic energy rises, so the molecules move faster on average.
Each molecule expands, so the gas now fills more of the container space.
They collide with one another less often, now that they have energy.

questions.explanation: The temperature of a gas is related to the average kinetic energy of its molecules, so raising the temperature raises that average and the molecules move faster on average.

questions.stem: Which statement about a gas and changes of pressure is correct?

options.text: A gas can be compressed or expanded by pressure changes.
A gas keeps a fixed volume whatever pressure is applied to it.
A gas can be expanded by pressure changes but never compressed.
A gas can only be compressed if it is squeezed from above.

questions.explanation: This is the specification statement: the molecules of a gas are far apart, so a change of pressure can squeeze the gas into a smaller volume or let it expand.

questions.stem: Where does the potential energy part of a system's internal energy come from?

options.text: From the speeds at which the particles are moving about inside
From the height of the system above the floor of the laboratory
From the positions of particles and the forces between them
From the temperature the system has been raised to

questions.explanation: Particles attract one another, so energy is stored in how they are arranged; that is the potential energy part.

questions.stem: Which word equation for the change in thermal energy is the one given in the specification?

options.text: change in thermal energy = mass × specific heat capacity × temperature change
change in thermal energy = mass × specific heat capacity × the final temperature
change in thermal energy = mass × specific latent heat × the temperature change
change in thermal energy = mass × specific heat capacity ÷ the temperature change

questions.explanation: This is the specification equation, written in symbols as ∆E = m c ∆θ.

questions.stem: In physics, what is meant by work?

options.text: Work is the energy stored inside a moving body.
Work is the transfer of energy by a force.
Work is a force acting over a given distance.
Work is the heating caused by a force.

questions.explanation: This is the specification statement: work is the transfer of energy by a force.

questions.stem: A cyclist uses a bicycle pump to inflate a tyre, and the barrel of the pump becomes noticeably warm. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: Friction between the piston seal and the barrel is the only cause of the warming.
Warm air is drawn in from outside, and that air heats the metal barrel.
Work is done on the gas as it is compressed, raising its internal energy.
The gas loses internal energy as it is squeezed, so heat is released.

questions.explanation: The piston exerts a force that moves, so work is done on the enclosed gas. That transfer increases the internal energy of the gas and can cause its temperature to rise.
